tools.name: login
tools.description: Authenticate with Corezoid. Supports two auth methods: (1) OAuth2 browser flow — opens a browser window and saves the token so it persists across sessions; (2) API key — provide api_login and api_secret to skip the browser flow (credentials saved to project .env). Optionally accepts account_url, workspace_id, and stage_id to skip interactive prompts.

api_login.description: API key login (alternative to OAuth2 browser flow). If both api_login and api_secret are provided, browser authentication is skipped.

api_secret.description: API key secret (alternative to OAuth2 browser flow). Must be paired with api_login. Stored in project .env — ensure .env is in .gitignore.

tools.name: logout
tools.description: Remove saved Corezoid credentials from disk.

tools.name: pull-process
tools.description: Export a single Corezoid process definitions to a JSON file. The file is saved to the folder path matching its location in Corezoid (resolved from parent_id).

tools.name: pull-folder
tools.description: Recursively export all processes from a Corezoid folder/stage to a local directory.

tools.name: push-process
tools.description: Validate and deploy a process file to Corezoid. Runs lint-process first and blocks the deploy on issues that would break it (broken node links, old-format nodes, RPC paths without reply, nodes missing a default go, sub-30s timers, literal reply values); advisory findings are shown but do not block. Active Call Process Stub Mode (obj_type:4) is allowed as a warning only when the target stage is resolved as mutable and non-production-like; immutable/prod/unknown stages are blocked because Stub Mode bypasses the real called process. Pass allow_active_stub_mode=true only after explicit confirmation that the temporary mock behavior is intentional. Pass force=true to deploy despite other blocking lint issues. Note: the server regenerates node IDs on every push and the local file is rewritten in place with the server's canonical scheme — reference nodes by title when iterating, and re-read the file after a push instead of reusing old node IDs.

allow_active_stub_mode.description: Explicitly allow deploying active Call Process Stub Mode (obj_type:4) when the target stage is immutable, production-like, or cannot be resolved. Use only after confirming that temporary mock replies are intentionally being deployed.

force.description: Deploy even if the pre-push lint finds generic blocking issues. Does not confirm active Stub Mode; use allow_active_stub_mode for that. Advisory findings never block. Default false.

process_path.description: Path to the process JSON file, relative to the project root (absolute paths are accepted when they point inside the project).

tools.name: lint-process
tools.description: Validate process structure. Reports orphaned nodes, noop conditions, unused set_params, passthrough escalations, shared error clusters (an error node fed by several different failing nodes — each needs its own Reply/Error cluster), old-format nodes (obj_type:0 err_node_id targets, or action logic mixed with go_if_const — the UI would force-convert the process), finals reachable without api_rpc_reply in a process that replies elsewhere (an RPC caller would hang), nodes whose logics do not end with a default go and time semaphors under the 30s server minimum (both reject the deploy), literal non-string values in api_rpc_reply res_data (a scheme shape that hangs the server commit on push), and active Call Process Stub Mode nodes (obj_type:4) that bypass the real called process.

process_path.description: Relative path to the process JSON file.

tools.name: run-task
tools.description: Run a task on an already-deployed Corezoid process (without re-deploying) and wait for it to reach a final node. Polls up to wait_sec (default 30), so tasks that cross async nodes (api, api_rpc, db_call, delay) still return their final result. On timeout reports the node the task is parked at, plus TaskRef/TaskID for follow-up via list-task-history.

data.description: JSON string with task input parameters

process_path.description: Relative path to the process JSON file.

ref.description: Optional custom task ref (lookup key, not a guaranteed idempotency key — duplicate-ref behavior depends on the target process/state-diagram). Use this to create a task with a specific, lookup-able ref — e.g. matching an external ID a downstream process keys off of. If omitted, an auto-generated ref ("<unix_ts>_<rand>") is used, same as before.

wait_sec.description: How long to wait (seconds) for the task to reach a final node before reporting it as in progress. Default 30, max 600. Raise it for processes with slow external calls or delay nodes.

tools.name: create-process
tools.description: Create a new empty process (conv_type "process") inside a Corezoid folder.

folder_id.description: Explicit Corezoid folder/stage ID to create in; overrides folder_path resolution

folder_path.description: Relative path to the folder directory. Omit to use the current directory.

tools.name: create-state-diagram
tools.description: Create a new empty state diagram (conv_type "state") inside a Corezoid folder. Use this for status / lifecycle storage instead of create-process.

folder_id.description: Explicit Corezoid folder/stage ID to create in; overrides folder_path resolution

folder_path.description: Relative path to the folder directory. Omit to use the current directory.

process_name.description: Name for the new state diagram

tools.name: create-folder
tools.description: Create a new folder inside a parent Corezoid folder.

folder_id.description: Explicit Corezoid folder/stage ID to create the folder in; overrides parent_path resolution

parent_path.description: Relative path to the parent folder directory. Omit to use the current directory.

tools.name: show-folder
tools.description: Show metadata for a single Corezoid folder: title, obj_type (0 normal, 2 project, 3 stage), parent folder ID and parent type.

tools.name: list-folders
tools.description: List the immediate children of a Corezoid folder (subfolders + processes + state diagrams). Lighter than pull-folder — does not write anything to disk.

folder_id.description: Corezoid folder ID whose children to list

tools.name: modify-folder
tools.description: Rename a Corezoid folder and/or update its description. At least one of title or description must be supplied.

tools.name: delete-folder
tools.description: Move a Corezoid folder to the recycle bin (Trash). Can be restored from the Corezoid UI.

tools.name: delete-process
tools.description: Move a Corezoid process (or state diagram) to the recycle bin (Trash). Can be restored from the Corezoid UI. Use pull-process first if you want a local backup before deleting.

tools.name: create-alias
tools.description: Create a short alias for a Corezoid process. Aliases are stage-scoped; the stage is derived from the process file's parent_id (walking up folders until a stage is reached), so a stale COREZOID_STAGE_ID in .env no longer produces the cryptic "Object is not in stage" error. Pass stage_id explicitly to override.

process_path.description: Relative path to the process JSON file.

short_name.description: Short alias name for the process

stage_id.description: Optional. Stage the alias should be created in. Defaults to the stage derived from the process file's parent_id, then to COREZOID_STAGE_ID from .env.

tools.name: create-variable
tools.description: Create an environment variable in a Corezoid folder.

stage_id.description: Root folder ID where the variable will be created

tools.name: list-variables
tools.description: List all environment variables (env_var) in a Corezoid stage: short_name, obj_id, data_type (raw/json), env_var_type (visible/secret), title, value and change time. Read-only. Secret variables are ALWAYS shown masked — their value is never retrievable after creation, only fingerprints. Returns the obj_id needed by modify-variable / delete-variable.

stage_id.description: Stage (root folder) ID to list variables from. Defaults to COREZOID_STAGE_ID from .env.

tools.name: modify-variable
tools.description: Modify a Corezoid environment variable: change its value, description (display title), data_type (raw/json), and/or rename it (new_name). CONSEQUENTIAL: renaming breaks every {{env_var[@old-name]}} reference in the stage's processes, and a value change takes effect immediately in running processes without redeploy. env_var_type (visible/secret) CANNOT be changed after creation — the server silently ignores such changes. Modify is partial: omitted fields keep their current value (a secret's value survives a modify that does not send value). SAFETY: apply=false (default) is a dry-run showing the current → new diff and, for renames, a local reference scan — nothing is changed. To apply you MUST show the diff to the user, get their explicit confirmation, then call with apply=true AND confirm="<short_name>#<obj_id>" (the CURRENT short_name, before any rename). Never modify a variable without the user confirming.

apply.description: false (default) = dry-run: show the current → new diff only. true = perform the modification (also requires a matching confirm).

confirm.description: Required when apply=true: must equal "<short_name>#<obj_id>" of the CURRENT variable (e.g. "payment-api-url#2192"). Guards against accidental and wrong-variable modifications.

description.description: New human-readable label (stored as the variable's title, same as create-variable). An empty string is ignored — titles cannot be cleared.

name.description: Current short_name of the variable (as used in {{env_var[@name]}}).

new_name.description: New short_name (rename). WARNING: breaks all {{env_var[@old-name]}} references — the dry-run reports affected local .conv.json files.

obj_id.description: Optional numeric variable ID (from list-variables). If given together with name, both must refer to the same variable.

stage_id.description: Stage the variable lives in. Defaults to COREZOID_STAGE_ID from .env.

value.description: New value. For data_type=json, a JSON-encoded string. Omit to keep the current value (secrets survive).

tools.name: delete-variable
tools.description: PERMANENTLY delete a Corezoid environment variable. DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE: unlike processes/folders/projects there is NO recycle bin for variables — the value (secrets included) is gone immediately, and any process still referencing {{env_var[@name]}} will fail at runtime. SAFETY: apply=false (default) is a dry-run that shows the variable's full details plus a local reference scan — nothing is deleted. To delete you MUST show the user the dry-run warning block VERBATIM, get their explicit confirmation, then call with apply=true AND confirm="<short_name>#<obj_id>". Never delete a variable without the user confirming.

apply.description: false (default) = dry-run preview only. true = perform the permanent deletion (also requires a matching confirm).

confirm.description: Required when apply=true: must equal "<short_name>#<obj_id>" (e.g. "stripe-key#2192"). Guards against accidental and wrong-variable deletion.

name.description: short_name of the variable to delete.

obj_id.description: Optional numeric variable ID (from list-variables). If given together with name, both must match.

stage_id.description: Stage the variable lives in. Defaults to COREZOID_STAGE_ID from .env.

tools.name: layout-process
tools.description: Auto-arrange a process's node coordinates into a clean, readable layout (waterfall for simple trees, layered+error-rail for meshes, aligned table/star grids for region bundles). Rewrites ONLY x/y; collapse/expand state, extra, edges, logic, conv_id and aliases stay intact. Runs entirely on the local file (no API, no auth). The result always reports the chosen strategy, canvas size and overlap count; dry=true previews placements without writing.

density.description: Spacing mode: compact | medium (default) | roomy (keeps the coarse block rhythm, skips compaction).

dry.description: Preview the planned coordinates without modifying the file.

process_path.description: Relative path to the process JSON file. Optional when the working directory contains exactly one .conv.json.

tools.name: list-workspaces
tools.description: Return the list of Corezoid workspaces (companies) available to the authenticated user.

tools.name: list-projects
tools.description: Return the list of projects inside a Corezoid workspace (company), sorted by title.

company_id.description: Workspace (company) ID whose projects to list

tools.name: list-stages
tools.description: Return the list of stages (environments) inside a Corezoid project.

company_id.description: Workspace (company) ID the project belongs to

project_id.description: Project ID whose stages to list

tools.name: create-project
tools.description: Create a new Corezoid project (with optional stages) inside a workspace. Returns the new project_id and the stage IDs that were created.

company_id.description: Workspace (company) ID where the project will be created

short_name.description: Project short name (alphanumeric, used in URLs). If omitted the server derives one from the title.

stages.description: Optional JSON array of stages to create with the project: [{"title":"production","immutable":true},{"title":"develop","immutable":false}]

tools.name: modify-project
tools.description: Update a Corezoid project's title, short_name and/or description. At least one of title/short_name/description must be provided.

company_id.description: Workspace (company) ID the project belongs to

tools.name: delete-project
tools.description: Move a Corezoid project to the recycle bin (Trash). Use restore-project to undo. Use destroy via the Corezoid UI to permanently delete.

company_id.description: Workspace (company) ID the project belongs to

tools.name: show-project
tools.description: Show a Corezoid project's metadata and the stages available to the caller. Returns project obj_id, short_name, parent folder ID and the list of stage IDs/titles.

company_id.description: Workspace (company) ID the project belongs to

tools.name: deploy-stage
tools.description: Deploy (promote) one stage's processes onto another within a Corezoid project — e.g. develop → production. Wraps the admin obj_scheme compare+merge that the UI "Deploy" button issues (on /api/2/compare and /api/2/merge). DESTRUCTIVE, and irreversible on an immutable target. SAFETY: apply=false (default) is a dry-run that only shows the diff and any conflicts — nothing is deployed. To actually deploy you MUST first get the user's explicit confirmation of the exact source→target, then call with apply=true AND confirm="<source_stage_id>-><target_stage_id>". Never deploy without the user confirming. The merge is asynchronous; this tool waits for it to finish over the progress WebSocket.

apply.description: false (default) = dry-run: show the diff/conflicts only. true = perform the deploy (also requires a matching confirm).

company_id.description: Workspace (company) ID the project belongs to.

confirm.description: Required when apply=true: must equal "<source_stage_id>-><target_stage_id>" (e.g. "684083->684082"). Guards against accidental and wrong-stage deploys.

project_id.description: Project ID that both stages belong to.

source_stage_id.description: Stage to deploy FROM (the source of truth, e.g. develop).

target_stage_id.description: Stage to deploy INTO (e.g. production). Its scheme is overwritten with the source's.

tools.name: set-stage-immutable
tools.description: Set a stage's immutable (read-only) flag. Immutable stages are the ONLY valid deploy/merge targets (see deploy-stage); an immutable stage can no longer be edited directly — only changed via deploy. Consequential: making a stage editable removes that protection. Requires explicit user confirmation — call with confirm="<stage_id>:<true|false>" (e.g. "684082:true"). Never change immutability without the user confirming.

company_id.description: Workspace (company) ID the project belongs to.

confirm.description: Required: must equal "<stage_id>:<immutable>" (e.g. "684082:true"). Guards against accidental read-only changes.

immutable.description: true = make read-only (a valid deploy target); false = make editable again.

project_id.description: Project ID the stage belongs to.

stage_id.description: Stage ID whose immutable flag to set.

tools.name: list-task-history
tools.description: Return the execution history (node path) for a task. Shows each node transition with node_id, node_prev_id, create_time_ms.

task_id.description: Task ID (obj_id) to retrieve history for

tools.name: list-node-tasks
tools.description: Return tasks currently sitting in a specific node of a process.

limit.description: Maximum number of tasks to return (default 50)

tools.name: get-node-stat
tools.description: Return time-series statistics (in/out counts) for a node over a time range. node_id is the ID shown in the Corezoid UI archive URL (/diagram/{node_id}/archive). ops[0]['data'] contains [{"date":"YYYY-MM-DD","in":N,"out":M}] for non-zero buckets. ops[0]['title'] is the node title.

end.description: Unix timestamp — end of the period

node_id.description: Node ID from the Corezoid UI archive URL

start.description: Unix timestamp — start of the period

timezone_offset.description: UTC offset in minutes, negative westward (e.g. -180 for UTC+3, default: 0)

tools.name: modify-task
tools.description: Modify an existing task's data. The task will continue from the node where it was paused with the updated data. At least one of task_id or ref must be provided.

data.description: JSON string with fields to merge into the task

tools.name: delete-task
tools.description: Delete a task from a process. At least one of task_id or ref must be provided. If only ref is given, the task_id and node_id are resolved automatically.

tools.name: create-dashboard
tools.description: Create a new Corezoid dashboard for visualizing process node metrics. Returns dashboard_id needed for adding charts.

folder_id.description: Folder (stage) ID where the dashboard will be created. Defaults to COREZOID_STAGE_ID from .env.

timezone_offset.description: UTC offset in minutes (e.g. -180 for UTC+3). Defaults to 0 (UTC).

tools.name: get-dashboard
tools.description: Get a Corezoid dashboard with its charts and series. Use after add-chart to verify series is populated.

tools.name: add-chart
tools.description: Add a chart to a Corezoid dashboard. chart_type must be one of: column, pie, funnel, table. Use 'column' for bar/comparison charts — 'bar' is not a valid type.

chart_type.description: Chart type: column, pie, funnel, or table

dashboard_id.description: Dashboard ID to add the chart to

tools.name: modify-chart
tools.description: Modify an existing Corezoid chart. Always provide the full series array — partial updates are not supported.

chart_id.description: Chart obj_id (hex string returned by add-chart or get-dashboard)

chart_type.description: Chart type: column, pie, funnel, or table

dashboard_id.description: Dashboard ID that contains this chart

tools.name: get-chart
tools.description: Get a single chart with its series data.

dashboard_id.description: Dashboard ID that contains this chart

tools.name: set-dashboard-layout
tools.description: Save chart positions on a dashboard grid. Must be called after add-chart/modify-chart to make charts visible. Each grid entry positions one chart by its chart_id (hex string from add-chart).

grid.description: JSON array of chart positions: [{"chart_id":"<hex>","x":0,"y":0,"width":6,"height":4},...]. Standard width=6, height=4. Grid is 12 columns wide.

timezone_offset.description: UTC offset in minutes (e.g. -180 for UTC+3). Defaults to 0.

tools.name: share-object
tools.description: Grant or revoke access to a Corezoid object (process/folder/stage/project) for a user, API key, or group. To revoke, pass privs="none" — that's the same wire operation as a share with empty privs. API keys share as obj_to="user" with the api key's obj_id.

notify.description: Send notification to recipient (default true). Ignored when revoking.

obj.description: Object kind: conv | folder | stage | project

obj_id.description: Numeric ID of the object being shared

obj_to.description: Recipient kind: user (includes API keys) | group

privs.description: Comma-separated list, JSON array, or keyword. Allowed values: view, create (task management), modify, delete, all (default), none (revoke all access).

tools.name: list-shares
tools.description: List users, API keys and groups that currently have access to a Corezoid object.

obj.description: Object kind: conv | folder | stage | project

tools.name: create-group
tools.description: Create a new user group in the current workspace. Returns the group's obj_id (use as obj_to_id when sharing).

tools.name: modify-group
tools.description: Rename a user group and/or update its description. At least one of title or description must be supplied.

tools.name: list-group-objects
tools.description: List the processes (conv objects) currently shared with a group. Used to audit group impact before destructive operations. Note: folders/stages/projects shared to the group are not retrievable via this endpoint.

tools.name: delete-group
tools.description: Delete a user group. By default refuses to delete if the group still has active shares — pass force=true to override. Existing share links are revoked when the group is deleted.

force.description: Delete even if the group still has active shares (default false).

tools.name: add-to-group
tools.description: Add a user (or API key user) to a group.

tools.name: remove-from-group
tools.description: Remove a user from a group.

tools.name: list-groups
tools.description: List user groups visible in the current workspace.

name.description: Optional substring filter on group title

tools.name: create-api-key
tools.description: Create a new API key in the workspace. The secret is written to ~/.corezoid/api-keys/<slug>-<obj_id>.json (mode 0600) and the chat output reports only the file path — the secret is never printed in agent responses.

tools.name: modify-api-key
tools.description: Update title and/or description of an existing API key. Does not regenerate the secret.

tools.name: delete-api-key
tools.description: Delete an API key. The secret is invalidated immediately — subsequent requests return 401. Objects owned by the key are reassigned to the workspace owner.

tools.name: list-api-keys
tools.description: List API keys visible in the current workspace.

name.description: Optional substring filter on key title

tools.name: find-principal
tools.description: Search users, groups or API keys in the workspace by substring. Returns obj_ids to pass as obj_to_id in share-object.

kind.description: What to search: user | group | api_key | shared. Defaults to user.

name.description: Substring to match against title (omit to list all)

tools.name: invite-user
tools.description: Invite an external email to the workspace AND share a process/folder/stage/project with them in one call. Returns the invite URL the recipient must open.

login_type.description: Login type: google | corezoid | phone (defaults to google)

obj.description: Object to share: conv | folder | stage | project

privs.description: Privs to grant (view, create, modify, delete, all). Defaults to view.

tools.name: send-feedback
tools.description: Submit user feedback about plugin behavior to Corezoid. Use only after the user has explicitly confirmed sending. Returns a feedback ticket id.

expected.description: What the user expected to happen.

problem.description: What went wrong, in the user's words.

proposed_solution.description: How the user thinks it should work.

tool.description: Tool or skill involved, if known.

transcript_excerpt.description: Short, already-redacted excerpt of the relevant dialog.

tools.name: create-snapshot
tools.description: Create a snapshot of the current server state of a process before making changes. Useful as a manual checkpoint before experiments. Auto-snapshot is also created automatically before every push-process on existing processes.

title.description: Optional snapshot title. Defaults to 'manual snapshot <ProcessName> <datetime>'.

tools.name: list-snapshots
tools.description: List all snapshots for a process. Returns version, title, author and creation time for each snapshot.

tools.name: delete-snapshot
tools.description: Delete a snapshot by its obj_id. Use list-snapshots to find the snapshot_id.

snapshot_id.description: The obj_id of the snapshot to delete (from list-snapshots).

tools.name: get-snapshot
tools.description: Get the node list of a specific snapshot for diff comparison against the current process state. Returns all nodes as they existed at snapshot time.

snapshot_id.description: The obj_id of the snapshot to retrieve (from list-snapshots).

tools.name: git-pull-context
tools.description: Clone or pull the Corezoid git mirror for the current workspace into .git-context/. Requires COREZOID_GIT_URL, API_LOGIN, and API_SECRET. Silently skipped if not configured.

tools.name: git-push-context
tools.description: Commit and push local _ext/ changes to the Corezoid git mirror. Requires API_LOGIN and API_SECRET. Returns a warning (not an error) if nothing changed.

commit_message.description: Optional git commit message. Defaults to 'docs: update _ext/ after task session <timestamp>'.

tools.name: read-context-file
tools.description: Read a file from .git-context/ of the current workspace (git mirror local copy). Returns content and a found flag.

tools.name: update-context-file
tools.description: Write or append to a file inside _ext/ of the git mirror local copy (.git-context/). Path must start with _ext/. Use git-push-context to publish the changes.

mode.description: Write mode: 'replace' (default) overwrites the file; 'append' adds to the end

path.description: Relative path inside .git-context/, must start with _ext/ (e.g. _ext/docs/context.md or projects/123/stages/456/_ext/docs/context.md)
